tools.name: sec_list_filings
tools.description: Free, no payment needed. Two uses: (1) with a ticker, CIK or company name, a US public company's 10-K (annual), 10-Q (quarterly) and 8-K (material event) filings from SEC EDGAR, newest first, back to 2001; (2) with no company, the latest filings across all companies from EDGAR's live feed (about the last few business days): "Which companies reported earnings since Friday?", "Who announced a CEO change today?", "Which 10-Qs were filed this morning?". Each filing has the company, ticker, form, filing date (and acceptance time in the live feed), sec.gov link, the sections sec_filing_section can extract (Risk Factors, MD&A, Business, Legal Proceedings, Market Risk, Cybersecurity) and the event items of each 8-K (earnings 2.02, executive changes 5.02, deals 1.01, cybersecurity incidents 1.05, …). Filter by form, 8-K `items` (codes or words like "earnings") and date. Every filing carries `next_call`: the exact paid tool call, with arguments and price, that returns its text. Up to 50 filings per call. Rate-limited per client.

ticker.description: US stock ticker, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK-B. Use this, `cik` or `company`; leave all three out for the latest filings of all companies.

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key, e.g. 320193. Use this, `ticker` or `company`.

company.description: Company name, e.g. "Apple" or "Coca-Cola". Use this, `ticker` or `cik`; a name matching several companies returns their tickers, free.

forms.description: Which filings to list: 10-K (annual), 10-Q (quarterly), 8-K (material events). Default: all three.

items.description: Only 8-Ks reporting any of these items, e.g. ["2.02"] for earnings, ["5.02"] for executive changes, ["1.05"] for cybersecurity incidents (words like "earnings" work too). Implies forms ["8-K"].

since.description: Only filings filed on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Reaches back to 2001 for one company; the market-wide feed covers about the last few business days.

limit.description: How many filings to return, newest first (1-50, default 20).

via.description: Optional: the tool whose next_calls suggested this call (filled in for you).

tools.name: free_sample
tools.description: Free, no payment needed. Returns a paid tool's real, live answer to its documented example input (refreshed every 5 minutes to 6 hours depending on the tool), the price of a call with your own input, and where to send it. With no `tool`, lists every paid tool with the URL of its sample. Use it to check a tool's output format and quality before paying, or to test an integration. Also answers GET, e.g. /api/v1/samples?tool=token_risk_check. Rate-limited per client.

tool.description: The paid tool to sample, by name or path, e.g. "token_risk_check" or "email-verify". Leave out to list every tool with its sample.

via.description: Optional: the tool whose next_calls suggested this call (filled in for you).

tools.name: token_launches_peek
tools.description: Free, no payment needed. Counts the pools created against WETH, ETH or USDC on Uniswap v2, v3, v4 and Aerodrome on Base since `since_block` (or in the last `minutes`) and how many distinct tokens they are for, by DEX, with the latest block. Counts only: the token addresses, names and risk verdicts come with the paid new_token_launches, whose ready-to-send call is included when there is something new. Built for polling bots: peek for free, pay only when new_tokens > 0. Rate-limited per client.

since_block.description: Only pools created after this Base block: pass the previous answer's latest_block when polling (at most 6 hours back).

minutes.description: How far back to look, in minutes (1-360, default 60). Ignored when since_block is given.

via.description: Optional: the tool whose next_calls suggested this call (filled in for you).

tools.name: sec_alert_subscription_status
tools.description: Free, no payment needed. Give the `subscription_id` and `signing_secret` from sec_alert_subscription to see whether it is active, when it expires, how many alerts were delivered and the last delivery error, or set `cancel: true` to stop deliveries (no refund).

tools.name: sec_alerts_peek
tools.description: Free, no payment needed. Counts the alerts sec_market_alerts would return for the same `since`, `levels`, `types` and `tickers`, by level and type, with a new `cursor`. Counts only: the companies, filings and excerpts come with the paid sec_market_alerts, whose ready-to-send call is included when there is something new. Built for polling: peek for free every few minutes, pay only when new_alerts > 0. Rate-limited per client.

since.description: Only alerts found after this time: pass the previous answer's `cursor` to get just what is new. Default: every alert in the store (about the last day).

levels.description: Only these levels: red (restatement, delisting, bankruptcy, late 10-K), amber, green (insider buying), info (earnings, leadership changes, deals). Default: all.

types.description: Only these alert types: bankruptcy, restatement, delisting_notice, late_annual_report, auditor_change, cybersecurity_incident, impairment, debt_acceleration, change_in_control, late_quarterly_report, insider_purchase, leadership_change, earnings, material_agreement, acquisition_or_disposal, restructuring, unregistered_share_sale. Default: all.

tickers.description: A watchlist: only alerts for these tickers. Default: the whole market.

tools.name: sec_filing_section
tools.description: Answers questions like "What are Tesla's risk factors?", "What did Apple's MD&A say about margins?" or "How has Microsoft's cybersecurity disclosure changed since 2023?". Returns exactly one section of a US public company's 10-K (annual) or 10-Q (quarterly) report from SEC EDGAR as clean text, ready for an LLM: Risk Factors (Item 1A), Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), Business, Legal Proceedings, Market Risk, or Cybersecurity. Look up by stock ticker or CIK. Defaults to the latest filing; pass `fiscal_year` (2001 on) for an earlier year's report, or `accession_number` for an exact filing (the free sec_list_filings tool lists them, with the sections each one has). For several sections of one filing use sec_filing_sections; for what changed since last year, sec_section_changes. The table of contents, page numbers, hidden XBRL data and HTML are removed; tables are kept as readable rows. Includes the filing date, fiscal period, accession number and sec.gov link for citation. Use it for investment research, due diligence, competitor analysis or risk monitoring without downloading a 100-page filing. Sections up to 200,000 characters. If the filing's item only points elsewhere ("See Note 12"), you get 404 SECTION_INCORPORATED_BY_REFERENCE with that pointer, free. You are only charged when a result is returned: invalid input (400) and upstream failures (4xx/5xx) are not settled. Costs $0.01 USDC per call via x402. Paid per call with x402 inside MCP (see the server instructions).

tools.name: sec_section_changes
tools.description: Answers "What changed in Tesla's risk factors this year?", "Which new risks did Apple add?" or "How did Microsoft's MD&A change since 2022?". Compares one section of a company's 10-K with the same section of an earlier 10-K from SEC EDGAR, paragraph by paragraph: paragraphs added (new risk factors appear here), removed, and edited, each edit with a word-level diff marking deletions [-like this-] and insertions {+like this+}, plus a summary (counts and the share of text unchanged). Moved but identical paragraphs count as unchanged. Defaults to the latest 10-K against the one before it; pass `fiscal_year` or `accession_number` for the newer report and `compare_to_fiscal_year` for the older one (2001 on). Sections: Risk Factors, MD&A, Business, Legal Proceedings, Market Risk, Cybersecurity (filed from late 2023 on). By ticker, CIK or company name, with sec.gov links for both filings. Use it for risk monitoring, due diligence and investment research without reading two 100-page filings. If either report lacks the section you get 404, free. You are only charged when a result is returned: invalid input (400) and upstream failures (4xx/5xx) are not settled. Costs $0.04 USDC per call via x402. Paid per call with x402 inside MCP (see the server instructions).

tools.name: sec_financials
tools.description: Answers "What were Apple's revenue and net income over the last five years?", "Is Tesla's free cash flow positive?" or "How fast is Nvidia growing quarter over quarter?". Returns a US public company's key financial-statement figures for its latest fiscal years (annual, from 10-Ks) or single quarters (quarterly), newest first, from the XBRL data companies file with the SEC: income statement (revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, R&D, SG&A, operating income, pretax income, tax, net income, basic and diluted EPS, diluted shares), balance sheet (cash, current and total assets and liabilities, long-term debt, equity) and cash flow (operating cash flow, capex, free cash flow, dividends, buybacks), plus gross, operating and net margins and year-over-year revenue growth. Fourth quarters and single-quarter cash flows, which companies only report as full-year or year-to-date totals, are derived and flagged in `derived`. Each period cites the latest filing that reports it, so restated figures replace original ones. Up to 20 periods per call, back to about 2009; `fiscal_year` reaches earlier years. By ticker, CIK or company name. US-GAAP filers only (not IFRS 20-F filers); values in USD. You are only charged when a result is returned: invalid input (400) and upstream failures (4xx/5xx) are not settled. Costs $0.005 USDC per call via x402. Paid per call with x402 inside MCP (see the server instructions).

tools.description: Answers "Are Nvidia's executives selling?", "Did any Intel insider buy shares on the open market this year?" or "What did Tesla's CFO do with his vested stock?". Returns a US public company's latest Form 4 filings from SEC EDGAR, the reports officers, directors and 10% owners must file within two business days of trading its stock: who traded (name, role, title), each transaction with its date, code and plain-English meaning, shares, price, dollar value, holdings after, and direct or indirect ownership, plus footnotes. Filter by filing date or transaction code (e.g. ["P"] for open-market purchases), optionally with option and RSU transactions; up to 40 filings per call. By ticker, CIK or company name. tools.name: scrape_markdown
tools.description: Use it when an agent needs to read a web page, article, documentation, PDF, blog post, product or pricing page, news story or RSS feed. Returns the main content as clean Markdown ready for an LLM: navigation, ads, footers and sidebars removed (or `mode: "full"` for the whole page), real tables as Markdown tables, code blocks with their language, math as TeX, the real (not lazy-loaded placeholder) images, absolute links without same-page anchors, and no needless escaping. Also returns metadata from meta tags and JSON-LD (description, author, published and modified time, language, site name, canonical URL, image, schema.org type), the HTTP status, word and token counts, and optionally the page's links. PDFs come back as text by page (up to 100 pages, 15 MB; no OCR), RSS/Atom feeds as item lists, JSON pretty-printed, and JavaScript-built pages that embed their content as data (JSON-LD articleBody, Next.js) are read from it. Long pages are returned in parts of up to 100,000 characters: pass `next_offset` back as `offset`; `strip_link_urls` saves tokens. Bot checks ("Just a moment...") and pages with no readable text answer 422 and are not charged; JavaScript is not executed. No account or API key. You are only charged when a result is returned: invalid input (400) and upstream failures (4xx/5xx) are not settled. Costs $0.002 USDC per call via x402. Paid per call with x402 inside MCP (see the server instructions).

tools.name: scrape_batch

Reads 2-5 public URLs in one paid call (one payment round trip instead of five), each exactly like scrape_markdown: the main content as clean Markdown (or `mode: "full"`), real tables, code blocks, metadata from meta tags and JSON-LD (author, dates, language, canonical URL), PDFs as text by page, RSS feeds as item lists, optionally each page's links.
